packs.title: Museums, public places and park paths
packs.promise: Compare real exhibits, make original pages and notice the city’s public settings.

q.s: Make an original little scene from an actual model-railroad run.
st: Enter the actual public run during its confirmed opening and stand in a permitted visitor viewing area. Watch a train moving through the model setting; no model detail or train is guaranteed.

Note one actual movement and two spatial relationships you can see, such as a train beside a structure or a track passing through planted scenery. Keep your notes descriptive rather than assigning a scale or prototype.
Use those observations to make an original six-line micro-story or a three-panel sketch on your own page. Change the characters and story; do not reproduce a model scene, sign or artwork exactly.
Keep the three observations and your original page. Move aside for notes and leave the model untouched; a conversation or a ride is unnecessary.

q.s: Collect the different edges of a short park view.
st: Choose a safe, open public-path-side position clear of active play and moving visitors. Stay on the path rather than entering planted areas or reserved spaces.

Collect three different visible edge or texture descriptions from this short area: one on the walking surface, one where the path meets its surroundings, and one farther away within an ordinary park view.
Compare the two easiest to distinguish. Explain which visible cue helped you tell them apart without guessing a plant species, material age or ecological process.
Keep three descriptions and the comparison. Collect observations only; no leaf, stone, wildlife sighting or photograph is needed.

q.s: Notice one detail from two directions on the same path.
st: Choose an open public path and record a simple visible start cue. Check actual conditions and remain within the park’s ordinary public walking scope.
Follow that same path for up to three minutes at an easy pace, turning earlier for conditions or comfort. Notice one ordinary path-edge detail without leaving the path.
Return along the same path to your start. Compare how the detail or its setting looked from the other direction; no fixed bend, sign or object is promised.
Write your start cue, actual outward time and comparison. Use the remaining time for notes and rest; no minimum distance earns extra credit.

packs.title: Downtown galleries and street scenes
packs.promise: Browse actual public interiors, create two street pages and finish with a park pause.

q.s: Collect shape relationships from an actual flower-shop display.
st: Enter the actually opened public retail area and choose a permitted place to view whatever flowers, containers or arrangements are currently displayed. No particular bloom, stock item or staff response is required.

Collect three visible shape relationships, such as tall beside low, open beside dense, or a container supporting a form. Describe what is actually present without assigning a species or copying a commercial arrangement.
Compare two relationships and explain which makes the display easiest for you to read. Keep the response about the display, not a review of the business or its service.
Keep the three notes and comparison. No purchase, touching, rearranging, photograph of merchandise or conversation is required.

q.s: Make an original composition from the theater’s exterior.
st: Choose a permitted public sidewalk position with a clear ordinary view of the theater exterior, keeping entries and pedestrian traffic clear.
Record two broad architectural shapes you can actually see, such as a vertical outline and a repeated facade line. Do not copy lettering, posters, artwork or decorative imagery.

Make an original small poster-like arrangement or six-line description using those shapes, with your own invented colors or layout. Do not use the venue’s name, branding, event text or an endorsement.
Keep the two observation notes and your original page. No performance, merchandise purchase, building entry or venue photograph is required.

q.s: Retrace a short public sidewalk and compare its cues.
st: At Main and Second, choose a safe start on the east-side public sidewalk clear of the corner and pedestrian flow. Record an ordinary visible start cue.

Walk on that same sidewalk toward First for up to three minutes, turning earlier as needed and always before the First Street crossing. Notice one path or building-edge cue without stepping into a doorway or road.
Return along the same sidewalk to your start. Compare how the cue helps you recognize the route from the reverse direction; no station access or railway crossing is needed.
Keep your start cue, actual outward time and comparison. A fixed distance, train sighting, ticket, platform board or ride is unnecessary.
